method.label: Use areas in the unit square

annotationRationale: Triangle inequalities and the cosine law define the favorable region. Uniform geometric probability then reduces the calculation to a quarter-circle area minus a triangle area.
sourceMethod: Followed the official unit-square area method, using the cosine law to explain the stated generalized Pythagorean comparison and verifying the containment needed for subtraction.

review.mathCheck: Within the unit square, triangle feasibility is exactly \(x+y>1\); obtuseness is additionally \(x^2+y^2<1\). The triangle below the diagonal lies wholly inside the quarter disk, so the favorable area is \(\pi/4-1/2\approx0.2854\), closest to 0.29, choice C. Degenerate and right-triangle boundaries have probability zero.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Originally worded, faithful adaptation of official solution 22 on page 10, matching its shaded region. The cosine-law sign calculation explains the official generalized-Pythagorean criterion, and the containment argument justifies subtraction.
review.annotationCheck: Both assessed nodes and all three supporting nodes match the worked steps. The explanation supplies the cosine formula and needs no numerical trigonometric evaluation.
